model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; adjusted common earnings after CET1 capital retention, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.item: Half the CET1 surplus above a 12.0% operating level
equity_bridge.note: (13.1% - 12.0%) x RWA C$492,866m = C$5,422m surplus at 31 Jul 2026 (BNS_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:114, :120); half credited because management is deploying it into buybacks (2026 NCIB) and U.S. growth (MapleMark), and OSFI can re-raise the DSB (range 0-3% after June 2026).

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: Free cash flow is not meaningful for a bank (OCF is deposit/loan movement); the FCF CAGRs are deliberately null. The distributable-earnings proxy is net income attributable to equity holders: FY2020 6,778; FY2022 9,916 (peak); FY2023 7,410; FY2024 7,758; FY2025 7,789 (reported, depressed by the ~C$1.4bn after-tax Colombia/CR/Panama held-for-sale impairment). Adjusted FY2025 ~C$9.5bn; FY2026E adjusted ~C$11.2bn.
historical_growth.revenue_series_note: FY2023 is as originally reported (32,307), not the IFRS 17 restated comparative (32,214), so FY2023->FY2024 growth compares slightly different bases. Common equity series (kpis TotalCommonEquity) used for equity CAGRs, not the preferred-inclusive shareholders_equity.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (5.0% FY27 tapering to 3.0%), anchored on the 5-year common-equity CAGR (4.1%) and the 9-year revenue CAGR (4.1%); the 3-year revenue CAGR (6.3%) is flattered by FY2025 FX and the BA-to-loan conversion.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGRs (3yr -10.9%, 5yr 1.4%) diverge >30% from the equity (4.1%) and revenue (3.8%) CAGRs: reported EPS is distorted by the FY2022 peak (benign credit, Canada Recovery Dividend tax not yet applied), the FY2023 Canada Recovery Dividend/tax-rate increase, and the FY2025 ~C$1.4bn divestiture impairment. Adjusted EPS grew 9.6% in FY2025 and ~+22% YTD FY2026 (6.35 vs 5.16). Growth is taken from the revenue and book-value series.

scenario_narratives.base: Scotiabank completes the North American pivot: Canadian Banking keeps its 19% ROE, wealth and capital markets grow faster than the loan book, and International Banking is a smaller, steadier Mexico/Peru/Chile franchise plus Davivienda and KeyCorp associate stakes. Revenue compounds at 5% fading to 3%, positive operating leverage takes the productivity ratio to ~51.5%, and credit normalises to ~54bp. Adjusted ROE settles near 15-16% (ROTCE ~18%) with roughly 70-80% of earnings distributed. At a 9.8% CAD cost of equity that franchise is worth ~2.4x tangible book, a little below the ~2.5x the market pays after the FY2025-26 re-rating: the price discounts the base case and a bit more.
scenario_narratives.bull: The pivot overdelivers: management's '14% is not a ceiling' proves right as U.S. commercial and deposit growth (MapleMark, KeyCorp) adds a third growth leg, productivity falls toward 49.5%, credit stays benign at ~50bp and the wealth mix lowers capital intensity. ROE reaches 16-17%, matching RBC-class peers. At a 9.8% cost of equity the bull value is only ~10% above the current price, so the market is already paying for much of this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: The tariff shock management stress-tests becomes the base: Canada stalls, Mexico contracts and Canadian mortgage renewals at higher rates push PCL to ~80bp for two years, NIM falls back toward 2.2% on rate cuts, and record capital-markets fees revert. Operating leverage turns negative and the productivity ratio drifts to ~54%. RWA migration absorbs capital and buybacks stop. ROE falls back to the 12-13% of the pre-pivot years - the bank's historical position as the weakest of the Big Six.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A Canadian D-SIB is valued on what it can distribute to common shareholders after funding the CET1 capital its risk-weighted assets require, discounted at a CAD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow (deposit and loan movement) and never with deposits, senior funding or subordinated debt treated as net debt. Adjusted common earnings are the flow, capital retention is the reinvestment, and preferred/AT1 distributions and NCI are charged inside the flow. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: with ROTCE rising from ~17% to ~18%, 3% terminal growth and a 9.8% cost of equity, the base is worth ~2.4x tangible book against the ~2.5x the market pays - roughly fair to modestly rich, with the bear case (ROE back to 12-13%) about 25% below the price and the bull about 10% above.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: every 10bp of PCL on ~C$770bn of loans is ~C$770m pre-tax (~5% of adjusted pre-tax income); Q2 FY26 ran at 66bp and the bear case uses ~80bp for two years
Net interest margin: 5bp on ~C$1.2tn of average earning assets is ~C$600m of revenue (~1.5%); NIM has expanded for five quarters and Bank of Canada / Banxico cuts point the other way
Canadian housing: mortgage renewals at higher rates with delinquencies already elevated in Q3 FY26
U.S. tariffs and Mexico: management's own pessimistic scenario (7.5% effective tariff on Canada/Mexico) and very pessimistic (3x, full retaliation) would move both PCL and growth
Capital: OSFI can raise the Domestic Stability Buffer back up from 3.0% (range 0-3%), and the CET1-surplus credit in the bridge assumes it stays deployable
FX: flows are CAD and the USD quote is converted at a dated CAD/USD rate; a 5% CAD move shifts the USD value ~5% with no change in the business
Strategic M&A: a larger U.S. acquisition (e.g. KeyCorp step-up) at ~1.5-2x book would change both capital and ROE; not modelled

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE BNS, USD regular close); 52-week range 62.98-95.74 USD. TSX BNS.TO and CADUSD=X fetched at the same time for the fx_note parity check.
data_sources.financials: BNS_Metrics.csv / BNS.duckdb (core_metrics + kpis, CAD millions, FY2016-FY2025 annual, Q1-Q3 FY2022-FY2025) - Revenue, NetIncome, TotalCommonEquity, NetInterestIncome, DividendsPaid, ShareRepurchases; FY2025 annual FS/MD&A (SBC at BNS_Annual_FY2025_FS.txt:645, share counts BNS_Annual_FY2025_MDA.txt:10310); Q3 FY2026 Quarterly Report to Shareholders (SEC 6-K accession 0001193125-26-364115, exhibit 99.1, fetched 2026-10-04 to research/BNS/Extracted/BNS_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt): T1 highlights (:84-160), T2 adjusted reconciliation (:182-227), capital and NCIB (:2329-2383), balance sheet (:2770-2800).
data_sources.qualitative: BNS_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): North America-first strategy, KeyCorp 14.9% stake, Davivienda divestiture (1 Dec 2025), MapleMark acquisition, medium-term targets (14%+ ROE, 7%+ EPS growth, positive operating leverage, 40-50% payout), risks.

sanity_check_review.outcome: tripped (exit 3) on 'Implied P/E 13.8x exceeds 2x the 10yr average 5.7x' -- judged a false trip; no valuation change made (fix_applied: none)
sanity_check_review.evidence: The check's historical_table prices are the NYSE USD close MULTIPLIED by inputs.fx_rate (CAD->USD 0.7019) instead of divided by it: FY2017 shows 45.29 where BNS closed ~US$64.5 / ~C$83 (64.5 x 0.7019 = 45.3). Every historical multiple is therefore understated by ~1/0.7019^2 = 2.03x. Corrected 10-year averages: P/E ~11.5x (max ~14.9x), P/B ~1.32x (max ~1.84x), P/Sales ~3.0x. The implied P/E 13.8x is within 2x of 11.5x and below the historical max; implied P/B 1.23x is below the corrected average. The trip comes from the check's FX handling on dual-currency tickers (quote USD, flows CAD), not from the drivers.
sanity_check_review.follow_up: scripts/sanity_check.py: historical price conversion for quote_currency != currency should divide by inputs.fx_rate (contract defines fx_rate as model -> quote). Needs a red-first test; out of scope for the dcf-analyst.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E adjusted total revenue (net interest income + non-interest income, before PCL; adjusting items are the Q1 FY26 Davivienda FX-translation release and acquisition-intangible amortisation). FY2026 ends 31 Oct 2026 and is unreported (annual due ~early Dec 2026). FY0 = 9M FY26 adjusted 30,465 (BNS_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:132) + Q4E 10,600 (Q3 run-rate 10,543, +0.5%). 9M reported 30,018 (:90). FY2025 reported was 37,741 (CSV). FY2026 is effectively post-divestiture: Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama left on 1 Dec 2025, so only November 2025 is in the base and the replacement ~20% Davivienda associate income is inside non-interest income. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027, ending ~13 months from the valuation date.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,219m common shares outstanding at 31 Jul 2026 (BNS_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:140, end of period) plus ~3m dilutive (Q3 average diluted 1,226m vs basic 1,223m, :138-139). NVCC conversion shares (4,707m at floor price, :2462) are EXCLUDED: they convert only at non-viability and their running cost (preferred dividends / LRCN and AT1 distributions) is charged inside the flow. Count held FLAT thereafter: equity-settled share-based payments are expensed in the flows, and the 2026 NCIB (15m shares, commenced 7 Apr 2026, :2382; 8.6m repurchased in Q3) is part of the distributed FCFE, so shrinking the count as well would count the buyback twice. Repurchases made Aug-Oct 2026 are not yet disclosed; refresh at the FY2026 annual.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. BNS is an OSFI-regulated Schedule I D-SIB: deposits (C$1,006bn at 31 Jul 2026, :106), senior bank debt (inside deposits) and subordinated debentures (~C$7.6bn, CSV total_debt) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and deposits with financial institutions (C$62.5bn, :102) are liquidity held against that funding, not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to COMMON equity at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Preferred shares and other equity instruments (C$9.9bn, :108) are charged inside the flow via their distributions, not in the bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = adjusted net income to common ~10,547 (9M 7,827 at :227 + Q4E ~2,720) less capital retained ~2,550 (6.2% of revenue: RWA +3.9% in 9M to C$492.9bn incl. FX, CET1 held 13.2% -> 13.1%). Cross-check: 9M FY26 capital returned C$6.3bn (dividends + buybacks, :4) = ~8.4bn annualised while CET1 slipped 10bp, i.e. distributions ran slightly ahead of organic FCFE. reported_fcf = FCFE + equity-settled SBC so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2019 -12,025; FY2020 +56,664; FY2025 +5,407) is deposit/loan/trading balance movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the equity-settled SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Equity-settled share-based payments C$15m FY2025, C$13m FY2024, C$14m FY2023 (statement of changes in equity, BNS_Annual_FY2025_FS.txt:645, :677; BNS_Annual_FY2024_FS.txt:702). The larger cash-settled plans (share-based payment expense ~C$407m FY2025, BNS_Annual_FY2025_MDA.txt:2247) are already inside non-interest expenses and therefore inside the pre-tax margin. House and street bases are near-identical (band collapses).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases C$895m (kpis); 2025 NCIB completed 20m shares at C$90.47 avg for C$1,846m by 6 Apr 2026 (:2383); 2026 NCIB up to 15m shares, 8.6m bought in Q3 FY26 (:3783). ~C$2.2bn is the 9M FY26 buyback implied by C$6.3bn total returned less ~C$4.1bn dividends. Not added to the flows: buybacks are a use of FCFE, not a source.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in CAD; the ticker BNS is the NYSE listing quoted in USD (1 NYSE share = 1 TSX common share, no ADR ratio). All values computed in CAD and converted at CAD->USD 0.7019 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, 2026-10-03T21:00Z). Parity check at the 2026-10-02 close: TSX BNS.TO C$129.93 x 0.7019 = US$91.20 vs NYSE US$91.19 (0.01% tie; proves rate, direction and quote basis). refresh_price.py moves the USD price but not this rate; re-date it on refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Total common equity C$79,212m at 31 Jul 2026 (:2797); goodwill and other intangibles C$16,012m (:2770) -> tangible common equity ~C$63.2bn = C$51.9/share on 1,219m; BVPS C$64.99 (:148). Preferred and other equity instruments C$9,939m and NCI C$1,471m (:2800) are excluded from the common base. Adjusted ROE 14.2% / adjusted ROTCE 17.2% in Q3 FY26, 13.5% / 16.3% YTD (:136-137). CET1 13.1% on RWA C$492.9bn (:114, :120). FY2026E adjusted common earnings ~10,547 / TCE 63.2bn = ~16.7% ROTCE.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in CAD, the currency of the flows: Government of Canada 10-year ~3.4% (Oct 2026) + beta 1.1 x Canadian equity risk premium 5.5% = 9.45%, plus 0.35pp for the emerging-market share of earnings (International Banking ~18-25% of earnings post-divestiture across Mexico, Peru, Chile, Caribbean, x ~1.5-2pp country premium) = 9.8%. Beta 1.1 (above NAB.AX's 1.0) for the LatAm mix and capital-markets income. One rate across all three scenarios; the credit cycle, tariff shock and Canadian housing risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a further premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial relative to C$79bn common equity; lease cost sits inside non-interest expenses and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-to-common flows. NCI income (9M FY26 C$94m, :194) and distributions on preferred shares / LRCN / AT1 notes (9M FY26 C$389m = adjusted NI to equity holders 8,216 less to common 7,827, :225-227) are removed INSIDE the flow through the 29.0% cash-tax-rate driver (adjusted effective tax ~24.3% + NCI ~0.9pp + preferred ~3.5pp + ~0.3pp GMT drift). Neither is deducted again in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity through the component engine, per the bank precedent (NAB.AX 2026-09-24, TFC 2026-10-02, USB, WFC, STT, NTRS, HBAN). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = growth x CET1 capital per unit of revenue is the clean-surplus equivalent and runs through the validated slider engine (which also writes the workbook). Engine mapping: revenue = adjusted total revenue; ebitda_margin_path = adjusted pre-tax income (revenue - adjusted non-interest expenses - PCL) PLUS equity-settled SBC, as % of revenue (FY2026E 36.1% = 100 - productivity ~52.8% incl. seasonally heavier Q4 - PCL ~11.1% [~61bp]); sbc_pct_path 0.04%; da_pct 0 (depreciation and software amortisation are inside non-interest expenses and are real costs for a bank); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to hold CET1 at a ~12.5% operating level as RWA grows with revenue = g x (RWA/revenue 12.0 x 12.5%) = 1.5 x g; cash_tax_rate_path = 29.0% (tax + NCI + preferred leakage); wacc = cost of equity 9.8%; net_debt 0. FY0 check: 41,065 x (36.1% - 0.04%) x (1 - 29%) = 10,513 vs adjusted common earnings ~10,547 (adjusted diluted EPS ~C$8.60). equity_bridge adds half the CET1 surplus above a 12.0% operating level (OSFI lowered the DSB to 3.0% on 19 Jun 2026, :2329, so the all-in minimum is 11.0%). KeyCorp (14.9%, equity-accounted) and Davivienda (~20%) earnings are inside non-interest income and therefore in the flows; their carrying values are NOT added in the bridge (that would count them twice). Residual-income cross-check: the base margin path lifts ROTCE from ~16.7% (FY2026E) to ~18% by FY2036 on a tangible base grown by retention; P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (18.0 - 3.0)/(9.8 - 3.0) = 2.2x x C$51.9 TBV = ~C$114/share, plus the C$2.2/share CET1 credit and the interim ROTE ramp, brackets the engine base of ~C$123 (2.4x TBV). Price is a regular close, not volatile. The Q3 FY2026 quarterly report (filed as 6-K exhibit 99.1, 25 Aug 2026) was fetched from EDGAR for this build into Extracted/BNS_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt; it is not yet in core_metrics (financial-parser should add Q1-Q3 FY2026).

bear.growth_rationale: U.S. tariffs escalate (management's pessimistic scenario), Canadian GDP stalls and Mexico contracts; Bank of Canada and Banxico cut harder, compressing NIM back toward the FY2024 ~2.2%; capital-markets fees revert from record levels. Revenue grows 2-3%.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27-28 PCL at ~14.5% of revenue (~80bp; FY2020 was ~1.0%), led by Canadian mortgage renewals (delinquencies already flagged elevated in Q3 FY26), unsecured retail and Mexico/Peru/Chile; productivity drifts to ~54% as revenue stalls against technology and AML spend: 100 - 54 - 14.5 = 31.5. Recovers only to productivity 53.5 / PCL 11.5 = 35.0 - roughly the FY2025 adjusted margin, i.e. the pivot's ROE gains are given back (adjusted ROE ~12-13%).
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = 1.5 x g, except FY27-28 held at 6.0% despite 2-2.5% growth because RWA migration (downgrades of performing loans) in a downturn consumes capital the model must top up before distributions.

base.growth_rationale: Adjusted total revenue. FY27 5.0%: NIM at 2.49% after five quarters of Canadian Banking margin expansion leaves less room to expand further, but loan growth ~4% (Canada modest, Mexico/U.S. commercial faster), Global Wealth Management AUM +16% YoY and record GBM underwriting give fee growth of 6-7%. Fades to 3.0% (Canadian nominal GDP ~3.5-4% less mature-market share), close to the 9-year revenue CAGR of 4.1%.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted pre-tax margin + equity-settled SBC on revenue. FY2026E 36.1% (productivity ~52.8%, PCL ~11.1% of revenue). Positive operating leverage (10 consecutive quarters, 9M FY26 +3.9%) takes the productivity ratio to ~51.5% by FY30 - short of management's ~45% aspiration, which the base does not grant - and PCL normalises to ~10.0% of revenue (~53-55bp of loans, FY2024 level): 100 - 51.5 - 10.0 = 38.5. That implies adjusted ROE ~15%, between the 14%+ target and Big Six peers' 15-17%.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~12.5% as RWA grows with revenue = 1.5 x g (RWA/revenue 12.0 x 12.5%). At 5% growth 7.5% of revenue (~C$3.2bn, ~29% of common earnings retained -> ~71% distributed as dividends at the 40-50% payout target plus buybacks); at 3.0% terminal growth 4.5% (~17% retained). Equivalent to g / ROTE at ~16-17% ROTE.

bull.growth_rationale: The North American pivot compounds: U.S. commercial and deposit gathering (MapleMark, KeyCorp partnership) adds a growth leg, wealth keeps double-digit AUM growth, Mexico benefits from near-shoring once tariff uncertainty clears, and NIM holds ~2.5%. Revenue grows 6.5% fading to 3.5%.
bull.margin_rationale: Productivity ratio reaches ~49.5% by FY31 (still above the 45% aspiration) and credit stays benign at ~9.5% of revenue (~50bp): 100 - 49.5 - 9.5 = 41.0. Implies adjusted ROE ~16-17%, in line with the best of the Big Six.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = 1.4 x g: the mix shift to wealth and fee income lowers RWA per dollar of revenue (RWA/revenue ~11.2 x 12.5%). Terminal 3.5% growth retains ~4.9% of revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: the shares re-rated from ~1.3x to ~1.9-2.0x book in twelve months on record results, PCL is still ~56-66bp with Canadian mortgage delinquencies flagged elevated, U.S. tariff policy is the bank's own named high-severity macro risk, and residual LatAm exposure (Mexico tariffs, Chile election, Caribbean hurricane damage) carries tail risk domestic peers lack. Bull cut to 25%: it requires cost-out, benign credit and a U.S. growth leg to all hold for a decade, and the ~14% ROE target was hit only in the latest quarter (YTD 13.5%). Matches the bank precedent (NAB.AX, TFC 25/50/25).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
